title: A week with an autonomous PR builder
tagline: Running an external autonomous builder (Obvious) on this pipeline for a week, with Claude Code as the reviewer of record.
why: A hackathon on 30 October came with an autonomous builder that opens pull requests by itself. The question was whether it could carry real pipeline work under real review, and what it would cost to keep.
mission: The builder took scoped specs and opened pull requests. Claude Code reviewed every one against the live system rather than the builder's own fixtures. Merges stayed with a person.
destination: A clear keep-or-drop call, and its unfinished work handed back to the in-house sessions.
showcase: Running an autonomous builder under independent review, and checking its work against production state rather than its own tests
Moving the merge gate into repository rules, so approvals are recorded where everyone can see them
Telling throughput from value: more pull requests is not more shipped value, so the call used the review results

milestones.title: Merge gate moved into repository rules
Decision: not keeping it after the trial
Trial ended; open pull requests handed back to in-house sessions

metrics.label: Pull requests merged in the pipeline repo
metrics.baseline: 8 over 23–29 Oct (7 days, before the builder)
metrics.current: 82 over 30 Oct – 6 Nov (8 days), 46 from the builder

source.label: GitHub pull-request history, by merge date

metrics.note: Throughput, not quality: six of the builder's pull requests were still open when the trial ended, and they went back to in-house sessions.

decisions.decision: Don't keep the builder after the trial.
decisions.why: Alex's call: its cost wasn't justified next to the in-house sessions, which already hold the production context.

decisions.decision: Enforce the merge gate in repository rules, not in any tool's own interface.
decisions.why: Approvals given inside the tool were invisible on GitHub, so the gate could drift without anyone seeing it.

log.text: Trial ended. Six open pull requests moved to the in-house queue.
Merge gate moved into repository rules.
